history.summary: PROVISIONAL RECORD: no web source documents any Hanuman temple in Churachandpur - its location, founding date and management are all unpublished and marked (verify) throughout this record. Targeted searches ("Hanuman" temple Churachandpur/Lamka) returned only Hanuman temples in other states/places (Boko and Cachar in Assam, Ratlam, Lucknow, etc.) and no Churachandpur shrine; the onefivenine Hindu-temples directories for Lamka/Saikot/Singngat/Henglep list no Hanuman temple in the district. What is verifiable is the local context: Churachandpur (Lamka) is the Kuki-Chin heartland, overwhelmingly Christian, with a small non-tribal Hindu community that maintains a handful of shrines (Meigeingakpa/Maigheingakpa temples in central Lamka, Shree Radha Krishna Mandir at Jangnomphai, Durga Temple at Saiton, per onefivenine). A Hanuman shrine serving this community may exist; nothing about it could be confirmed online. Do not invent a location or founding date - this entry must be verified on the ground before use. town_description: Churachandpur (locally called Lamka) is the second-largest town of Manipur and the headquarters of Churachandpur district, about 60 km southwest of Imphal on Tiddim Road. It is the heartland of the Kuki-Chin hill tribes (Thadou-Kuki, Hmar, Paite, Zou) and is overwhelmingly Christian; a small Hindu/Meitei community maintains a handful of shrines in and around the town. Khuga Dam, about 12 km south, is the district's main reservoir and picnic viewpoint.
